ArenaNet unveil the future of competitive Guild Wars 2 with Pro Leagues

The question is, will the esports world bite this time? This has been ANet's goal since before launch, but previous efforts have failed to gain serious traction. The combat system was certainly designed from the start to be centered around PvP, and there's certainly a core demographic that appreciates this, but this isn't their first attempt to appeal to this crowd (that expands beyond players, to spectators as well).

Colin is a great guy, and so are a lot of the devs there, so I wish them well. That said, I still feel some of the concerns addressed in the comments at the end of the article are quite relevant. Spell-effect spam in particular can hamper the viewing experience. You have to basically ignore the spell effects (of which there are many) and just watch the little red or green rings on the ground to know what's going on. And the AoE rings are not as noticeable or informative in GW2 as they are in some other MMOs, notably Wildstar and FFXIV. An AoE ring overhaul would take a lot of work, but IMO could be worth the effort. Like, the other 2 MMOs I mentioned have a variety of styles for the AoE rings, and they look different when an AoE is about to go off (expanding rings vs just a red ring being there or not).

I wound up getting pretty burnt out on the PvE aspect of the combat, a lot of the weapon sets aren't very interesting in that area and there is a lot more 1-spamming than in other MMOs. That said, the 1-spamming isn't so boring/annoying in pvp because the utility skills that take up the rest of those slots are suddenly a lot more important.

In my experience the 1-spam was really only a thing against the basic world bosses like the Jungle Wurm or the Shadow Behemoth.

More complex world bosses require a bit of coordination, and even then the world boss system was only a part of PvE in the game, dungeons require some skill and knowledge (at least besides the paths that people have gotten down to speedruns) and I have high hopes for the more advanced content in the expac.
